text:
sam: Doing porch WFH for the first time this summer. Great breeze, terrible Zoom. Router's in the kitchen two rooms away. Posted a pic: https://files.slack.com/archives/random/FPORCH/IMG_20260707.jpg

jamie: Love the vibe. Quick test: move your laptop to 5GHz and sit near the sliding door. Distance kills throughput.

maya: If you need stability for the call, tether to your phone as hotspot, plug phone into power, and disable wifi on the laptop so it doesn't try to jump back.

sam: Hotspot helped for audio but demo video still lagged. Any cheap hardware I can drop today?

lee: Travel router or USB3-to-Ethernet + long cable to a window are the fastest. I once used a 15ft ethernet and taped it under the door for a deck demo.

it-bot: Tip: "Powerline adapters can be hit-or-miss depending on wiring. If you try them, pair identical brand adapters and avoid going through surge protectors when testing." :robot_face:

cora: Also check for background uploads (Dropbox/Drive). Pause them. And try lowering Zoom to 360p/turn off HD. Audio-first.

sam: Good call on Dropbox  it was mid-sync and chewing bandwidth. Paused and things improved. Cat then jumped on my keyboard and unmuted me mid-meeting  joy. Posted the unmuted-photo for shame. :cat:

jamie: Classic. Use a keyboard cover or quick toggle mute shortcut (I put it on F8). Also consider a small directional USB mic close to your mouth; cuts porch noise.

maya: If this is recurring, an outdoor-rated AP aimed at the porch is worth it. Otherwise, a travel AP + cheap directional patch cable will do for weekends.

sam: Thanks everyone. For now: hotspot, paused sync, directional mic on order, and a stern talk with the cat. Will post victory pic if the demo survives. :sweat_smile:
